# Entanglement Assistance Output Limits

> A uniform output-dimension bound on the classical communication advantage of unlimited preshared entanglement for finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channels.

## Scientific question and result

For a channel T:A→B, let b=rank T(I_A) be its effective output-support dimension and r the real affine dimension of its output-state image. The central estimate is C_E(T)≤16br χ(T)≤16b(b²−1)C(T). It is uniform over all finite input dimensions and arbitrarily small output eigenvalues. The complete theorem and proof, including zero-capacity cases, live in the scientific pages below.

## Distinctions to preserve

- C(T) is the regularized ordinary classical capacity. Do not replace it by the single-use Holevo quantity χ(T) for an arbitrary channel; the proof uses χ(T)≤C(T).
- C_E(T) allows unlimited preshared entanglement. The dimension b counts the channel output alone, not the receiver's stored entanglement or the reference system.
- The result ranges uniformly over every finite input dimension. It does not assert an infinite-dimensional input extension.
- Use the capacity inequality when C(T)=0. A ratio is only defined when the denominator is positive.
- The BKM metric is evaluated on the effective support and, for Schmidt decompositions, on the support of the input marginal. The compressed square (PHP)² and the compression PH²P need not coincide.
- A genuine fixed-input-basis classical stochastic channel has no entanglement-assisted gain. Classical output alone does not imply this; the trine measurement example has a gain.
- Fixed output dimension with weak depolarizing signal and growing output dimension at the negative complete-positivity boundary are different limits. The latter has ratio 2b+4/3−4/(9b)+O(b⁻²).
- The universal factor is a proved bound, with no claim that its constant or cubic dimension dependence is optimal. Known examples require at least linear dimension growth.
- Finite computations check calculations and conventions. The analytical proof establishes the general result.
